experiment_description: Bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) pulses were generated by collinear, frequency-degenerate type-I spontaneous parametric down-conversion in two 2-mm-thick beta-barium borate (BBO) crystals placed symmetrically about the common focus of an f = 1000 mm lens. The pump was an amplified Ti:sapphire femtosecond laser at 800 nm central wavelength, 25 fs pulse duration, 3 kHz repetition rate, with tunable single-pulse energy up to about 700 µJ. The BBO crystals were angularly tuned for phase matching near 1600 nm. A long-pass filter with 1180 nm cutoff removed residual 800 nm pump light, and an f = 600 mm lens collimated the BSV. For photon-statistics characterization, a low-reflectivity glass plate picked off a fraction of the BSV beam immediately after generation and sent it to a near-infrared spectrometer covering 1000–2500 nm. For each BSV intensity setting, spectra from 20,000 consecutive pulses were recorded. The photon number per pulse was computed from the measured spectrum I(lambda), spectrometer response S(lambda), and glass-plate reflection coefficient R as an integral proportional to (1/R) times I(lambda)/S(lambda) over wavelength. The second-order intensity correlation was extracted in the large-photon-number limit from the pulse-to-pulse photon-number distribution. The BSV average pulse energies used for the characterization were 3.3 µJ, 5.0 µJ, 8.3 µJ, and 10 µJ, corresponding in the ionization geometry to average peak intensities of 0.53, 0.80, 1.33, and 1.60 × 10^14 W/cm^2, respectively.

second_order_correlation_g2_at_3p3_uJ.description: Measured zero-delay second-order intensity correlation of the BSV photon-number distribution for the 3.3 µJ average pulse-energy condition.

second_order_correlation_g2_at_5p0_uJ.description: Measured zero-delay second-order intensity correlation of the BSV photon-number distribution for the 5.0 µJ average pulse-energy condition.

second_order_correlation_g2_at_8p3_uJ.description: Measured zero-delay second-order intensity correlation of the BSV photon-number distribution for the 8.3 µJ average pulse-energy condition.

second_order_correlation_g2_at_10_uJ.description: Measured zero-delay second-order intensity correlation of the BSV photon-number distribution for the 10 µJ average pulse-energy condition.

experiment_description: The temporal envelope of the generated 1600 nm BSV pulses was characterized at the input of the strong-field interaction region using frequency-resolved optical gating (FROG). The BSV beam was redirected into the FROG apparatus with a flipping mirror, split by a polarizing beamsplitter into two orthogonally polarized arms, recombined at a second polarizing beamsplitter, and focused into a BBO crystal for second-harmonic generation. The relative delay between the two arms was scanned while recording the second-harmonic spectra; the displayed FROG spectrogram covered delays from roughly 0 to 150 fs and second-harmonic wavelengths near 700–850 nm. A standard retrieval algorithm was used to reconstruct the temporal intensity envelope, and the full width at half maximum was obtained from the retrieved profile.

bsv_pulse_duration_fwhm_fs.description: Full width at half maximum of the reconstructed BSV temporal intensity envelope at the input of the interaction region.

experiment_description: Strong-field ionization of xenon atoms was performed with BSV driving pulses in a Cold Target Recoil Ion Momentum Spectroscopy (COLTRIMS) apparatus. The BSV pulses were centered near 1600 nm and generated by the double-BBO type-I SPDC source pumped by 800 nm, 25 fs, 3 kHz Ti:sapphire pulses. The BSV pulses were focused into a pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet inside a high-vacuum chamber maintained at 5 × 10^-11 mbar using a concave mirror with 75 mm focal length. The xenon backing pressure was 0.7 atm. Electrons produced by ionization were extracted and guided by calibrated electric and magnetic fields to a microchannel-plate detector with delay-line readout, giving time- and position-resolved single-electron detection and reconstruction of three-dimensional electron momenta. Millions of events were accumulated for each condition. The BSV average pulse energies were swept over 3.3, 5.0, 8.3, and 10 µJ, corresponding to average peak intensities of 0.53, 0.80, 1.33, and 1.60 × 10^14 W/cm^2. The measured photoelectron momentum distributions were analyzed in the px–pz projection for the presence or absence of above-threshold-ionization intercycle peaks/rings and intracycle spider-like holographic fringes from indirect–forward-scattered electron trajectory interference.

ati_peaks_suppressed_for_all_bsv_energie.description: Whether above-threshold-ionization peak/ring features were suppressed in the measured BSV-driven xenon photoelectron momentum distributions throughout the tested BSV pulse-energy range.

spider_like_holographic_fringes_present_.description: Whether spider-like holographic interference fringes were observed in the measured BSV-driven xenon photoelectron momentum distributions throughout the tested BSV pulse-energy range.

experiment_description: A direct comparison of xenon strong-field ionization by bright squeezed vacuum and by coherent-state mid-infrared light was carried out in the same COLTRIMS geometry. For the BSV case, 1600 nm BSV pulses with 10 µJ average pulse energy and 1.60 × 10^14 W/cm^2 average peak intensity were focused into the pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet. For the coherent-state case, the BSV beam was replaced by 1600 nm coherent-state pulses from an optical parametric amplifier pumped by the same Ti:sapphire laser system; these pulses passed through the same optical path and were focused onto the xenon target with the same geometry at 1.0 × 10^14 W/cm^2 intensity. The chamber pressure, xenon backing pressure, electron extraction fields, and MCP delay-line detection scheme were the same as for the BSV ionization measurements. Three-dimensional photoelectron momenta were reconstructed event-by-event and plotted as pr versus pz, where pr is the radial transverse momentum defined by pr = sqrt(px^2 + py^2), with px and py the two momentum components transverse to the laser polarization and pz the momentum along the laser polarization. The distributions were analyzed for above-threshold-ionization rings, carpet-like interference patterns, and spider-like holographic fringes.

bsv_10_uJ_spider_like_holographic_fringe.description: Presence of spider-like holographic interference fringes in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by 10 µJ BSV pulses.

bsv_10_uJ_ati_rings_observed.description: Presence of pronounced above-threshold-ionization rings in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by 10 µJ BSV pulses.

bsv_10_uJ_carpet_like_interference_obser.description: Presence of carpet-like interference structures in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by 10 µJ BSV pulses.

coherent_1600_nm_ati_rings_observed.description: Presence of pronounced above-threshold-ionization rings in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by the 1600 nm coherent-state driving field.

coherent_1600_nm_carpet_like_interferenc.description: Presence of carpet-like interference structures in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by the 1600 nm coherent-state driving field.

coherent_1600_nm_second_order_correlatio.description: Measured zero-delay second-order intensity correlation of the coherent-state 1600 nm driving light used for the xenon ionization comparison.
